Subject: [Status] Intermittent SSL handshake failures impacting hosted API (US-WEST) - Borealis Supply

Hi Lena / Borealis on-call,

Quick note: we are observing intermittent SSL/TLS handshake failures for a subset of requests routed to our US-WEST (usw1) edge cluster starting ~08:50 PDT. Symptoms: elevated connection resets and 502/524 responses on generation endpoints, increased client retry rates. We have flagged this as a Sev 2 impacting some customer traffic in the region.

What we’re doing now:
- Redirecting new sessions away from the affected small subset of edge nodes.
- Pulling handshake traces and TLS metrics; attaching a brief snapshot for your team.
- Engaging infra & network (cc Ben & Monica) to validate cert chain and ALB config.

Workaround for Borealis: If you can temporarily prefer region us-east (use region=use1 in routing) your incoming calls should avoid the nodes we’re isolating. If you need us to coordinate a configuration toggle on our side we can do that quickly.

Status page: https://status.redwood.inference/incidents/2025-07-30-usw1-ssl-handshake (we’ll update this as we have more info).

ETA next update: 30 minutes. Sorry for the disruption — we know this impacts your workflows.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: incident_snapshot_20250730.json (small), handshake-trace-usw1.txt

Subject: Re: [Status] Intermittent SSL handshake failures impacting hosted API (US-WEST) - Borealis Supply

Hi all — final update and short postmortem notes for Borealis: we completed a rolling mitigation and validation and have moved the affected nodes into maintenance mode. Root cause: a control-plane certificate renewal job deployed an intermediate cert bundle with an unexpected ordering for one small subset of edge proxies; most clients tolerate the chain but some client stacks (and our ALB health checks) rejected the reordered chain which produced handshake failures for ~3% of US-WEST connections between 08:50 - 11:05 PDT.

What we did:
- Isolated and drained 6 edge proxies that served the mismatched bundle.
- Reapplied the cert bundle with correct ordering and ran a full handshake sweep.
- Validated sticky/session_id affinity behavior by sending synthetic sessions for Borealis — confirmed session affinity is preserved when we rerouted to use1.
- Issued a configuration guard to prevent automatic rollout of cert-bundle changes to edge proxies without canary verification.

Customer impact: brief intermittent 502/524s and elevated retries; error window ~2h15m peak, full mitigation by 11:05 PDT. We will publish the full postmortem to the incident doc link below once internal review is complete.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-borealis.pdf (draft)
Status page: https://status.redwood.inference/incidents/2025-07-30-usw1-ssl-handshake

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll follow up with the finalized postmortem and notes on the guardrail changes.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
